repository_paths: Relative to the igris_c_isaacsim_public workstation checkout; provenance only.

ik/pink/servo_factory.py.change: Reads the native solver from the shipped runtime (the upper_body_control.py bytes before the backend hook, whose hash equals the production solver) instead of a separate reference copy; the per-solve experimental diagnostics key was removed (the runtime client adds 'ik_backend'). Same Pinocchio kinematics, Pink QP adapter, objective and integration.

ik/pink/worker.py.change: Same JSON-lines protocol and stop-on-first-error policy, plus: hello handshake (interpreter, exact package versions, worker source hashes), one runtime profile per worker, protocol kept on a private file descriptor (library output goes to stderr), SIGINT ignored, owner watchdog, and the --check self-test used by setup.sh/check_release.py.

runtime/{profile}/source/robros_motion_p.change: WorkerClient/proxy part only (the experiment launcher and its guards are not shipped): explicit NEPES_IK_BACKEND selection (default pink), NEPES_IK_PYTHON discovery with a clear error, version/source/limits verification, run report, no fallback and no restart.
The production file followed by a short import-time hook (no absolute paths). The part before the hook marker is byte-identical to the production solver.

requirements/ik_pink.txt.change: Complete runtime closure of the validated environment pinned exactly; pytest removed.

limitations: One paired trial per arm, baseline always first; cache/order/system load may explain differences. This is not a reliable speedup estimate.
Measured wall includes real Pink stdio-worker overhead and full capture/storage export, not pure solver arithmetic.
Throughput sections nest; never sum environment_step_including_capture with capture_render_and_read/all_render_calls.
Exact equality of these recorded trajectories does not establish success probability or equivalence across other seeds.
Benchmark output remains experimental and is excluded from production dataset quotas.
